/-!
# Ben Green's Open Problem 7

Does Ulam's sequence have positive density?
Can one explain the curious Fourier properties of Ulam's sequence?

*References:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 7](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.1)
- [erdosproblems.com/342](https://www.erdosproblems.com/342)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Nat Set Filter
open scoped Topology

namespace Green7

/--
Does Ulam's sequence have positive density?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 42]
theorem green_7.variants.positive_density :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, Erdos342.IsUlamSequence a →
        Set.upperDensity (Set.range a) > 0 := by
  sorry

end Green7

reformulations.difference: Relative to the second cited source, Erdős 342, which asks 'Is the density 0?', the Lean statement asks whether the Ulam sequence has positive upper density. Green's own question uses the unqualified phrase 'positive density'.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For any S ⊆ ℕ, its counting proportions lie in [0,1]. Consequently S has natural density zero iff its upper density is zero, and positive upper density is exactly the negation of natural density zero. IsUlamSequence fixes the standard sequence uniquely; it is inhabited by the greedy construction, since the sum of the two largest entries of any positive increasing prefix is uniquely representable and exceeds the last entry. Thus quantification over all sequences satisfying the predicate is harmless. The answer slot is answer(sorry), so negating the cited zero-density question simply reverses the eventual answer. The scratch file proves the density equivalence, sequence uniqueness, and the quantified equivalence given a sequence witness; the full infinite-sequence existence construction was not formalized.
